Two positive-form Cauchy--Schwarz estimates give the global defect bounds m/sqrt(M) and M/sqrt(m). Spectral subspaces near the two endpoints and a second-order expansion force both constants to be optimal, including when the spectral endpoints are not eigenvalues. The scalar-spectrum case is handled separately. The cited paper supplies exactly the intrinsic-part criterion and metric formula needed after these constants are established.

value.rationale: The result identifies a natural complete metric subgeometry of the newly introduced intrinsic norm cone: every Hilbertian renorming lies in one intrinsic part, and the entire restricted metric is exactly a fixed factor of the familiar symmetric log metric. The sharp constants are dimension-free and remain valid in infinite dimension with continuous spectrum, so this is more than a single finite-dimensional example or a routine parameter substitution.
